newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia interbank rates fall on fresh liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia interbank rates fall on fresh liquidity.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates fell sharply due to fresh liquidity in the market, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said one-week money dropped to 6.80/90 percent from 7.70/80, two-week money to 6.90/00 from 7.60/70 and one-month at 7.15/20 against 7.35/40.
Dealers said they were not sure of the source of funds which came into the market late on Tuesday and pushed down the overnight rate to 6.00 percent from 8.5 on Monday.
"Nobody seems to know where the liquidity has come from. We can only guess," a dealer with a local bank said.
Some dealers said it was foreign banks which introduced the fresh liquidity, though they did not know where these banks got their funds from.
Others said it was possible that a large overseas payment came into the market, like petroleum royalty. There were no maturities of any government bonds or deposits.

"The timing of the funds inflow was perfect to push rates lower. The volume could not have been more than a couple of million ringgit, but the effect was strong because the market was so tight," said the head of money dealing at a large bank.

The interbank market had been tight for over two weeks due to withdrawal of funds by overseas investors as calm returned to some of the troubled Southeast Asian markets and a large borrowing by Bank Negara at its last open market intervention.

The central bank regularly intervenes in the market to keep a check on liquidity or set interest rates, either through open tenders or by siphoning off funds directly from principal dealers. Its last intervention was on August 23.
